Summary  
Data source overview: The article explains how empirical “scaling laws” guide the allocation of limited compute between model size, dataset size and training duration.  It describes the 2020 OpenAI scaling law which favoured increasing parameter count, and the 2022 DeepMind revision which shows that holding compute fixed, proportionally increasing both data and parameters (the “Chinchilla” recipe) yields much higher performance.  
EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[88]  
Inference strategy justification: The text rarely uses formal section headings, so node rationales reference the closest descriptive paragraph (e.g. “OpenAI 2020 scaling laws paragraph”).  Moderate, clearly-flagged inference was applied only where the safety-relevant intervention (“Adopt compute-optimal scaling strategy …”) is implicit rather than explicitly instructed.  
Extraction completeness: All causal-interventional paths from the top-level risk (sub-optimal performance & wasted compute) through problem analysis, two competing theoretical insights, design rationale, implementation mechanism, validation evidence and the actionable intervention are captured.  Every node is connected and no intervention attaches directly to the risk node.  
Key limitations: 1) The source is short and non-technical, so edge confidences rely mainly on empirical claims in cited papers, not original statistical detail. 2) Environmental or broader safety implications of inefficient scaling are not deeply articulated in the text and thus are not modelled here. 3) Future work could add separate pathways for environmental impact risks if another source supplies quantitative evidence.
